ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a benzo-fused five-membered nitrogen-containing ring skeleton, with a nitrogen atom labeled N-H inside the ring; the ring carbon on the right is connected to both an H and an NMe2 substituent. There are two curved arrows in the figure: one points from the right C-H bond to the adjacent intraring bond position, and the other points from the C-NMe2 bond toward the NMe2 nitrogen atom. Then reasoning: According to the electron movement indicated by the arrows, the C-H bond electron pair enters the adjacent skeleton to form a C=C/conjugated fragment; the C-NMe2 bond electron pair moves onto the dimethylamino nitrogen, causing NMe2 to detach from the main skeleton. The benzene-ring fused structure and the intraring N-H connectivity remain unchanged, and the remaining main skeleton corresponds to the SMILES c1(C=CN2)c2cccc1.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows an indoline/indole-like benzofused five-membered ring with an N-H atom in the ring and a right-side carbon attached to H and NMe2. Follow the curved arrows exactly: move the C-H bond electron pair into the adjacent ring bond to create the alkene/conjugated C=C fragment, and move the C-NMe2 bond electron pair onto the dimethylamino nitrogen, removing NMe2 from the main skeleton. Keep the benzene fusion and the ring N-H connectivity unchanged. Convert the remaining fused heterocycle into SMILES, yielding c1(C=CN2)c2cccc1.
